title: QUIZ - 17
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.concept: Comparing Percentages Given in Different Forms
questions.learningObjective: Compare a percentage to a fraction expressed as a percentage
questions.question: Which represents a larger portion of a whole: 15% or \( \frac{63}{100} \)?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{63}{100} \) equals 63%. Comparing 15% and 63% shows 63% is larger.
questions.hint: Convert every value to the same form (a percentage) before comparing.

questions.concept: Ranking Multiple Percentage-Based Quantities
questions.learningObjective: Rank several quantities computed from different percentages and totals
questions.question: City B has 36% of its 1143 residents as commuters, City C has 30% of its 4526 residents as commuters, and City A has 12% of its 4699 residents as commuters. Rank the cities from most to fewest commuters.

options.label: A
options.text: City B, City A, City C

options.label: B
options.text: City B, City C, City A

options.label: C
options.text: City C, City A, City B

options.label: D
options.text: City A, City B, City C

questions.explanation: City B: 36% \(\times 1143 = 411.48\), City C: 30% \(\times 4526 = 1357.8\), City A: 12% \(\times 4699 = 563.88\). Ranking these commuter counts from greatest to least gives City C, City A, City B.
questions.hint: Compute the actual commuter count for each city, then rank the resulting numbers.

questions.concept: Comparing Percentages of Different Totals
questions.learningObjective: Compare two percentage-based quantities computed from different totals
questions.question: Store A reports that 20% of its 102 items are on sale, while Class Y reports that 20% of its 209 items are on sale. Which store has more items on sale?

options.label: A
options.text: Both stores have the same number of items on sale

questions.explanation: Store A has 20% of 102 = 20.4 items on sale, and Class Y has 20% of 209 = 41.8 items on sale. Comparing 20.4 and 41.8 shows Class Y has more.
questions.hint: Calculate the actual number represented by each percentage before comparing.
